description: An individual signer's signature on an `com.etzhayyim.esign.envelope`. The signer authenticates with a WebAuthn passkey (ES256 or EdDSA) bound to their DID via the DID key registration; the WebAuthn assertion (clientDataJSON + authenticatorData + signature) is recorded for non-repudiation. The encrypted assertion bytes use the Signal key-wrap envelope per ADR-2605181100. Append-only — declines use `com.etzhayyim.esign.declineEnvelope` instead.

envelopeUri.description: AT URI of the `com.etzhayyim.esign.envelope` being signed.

signerDid.description: DID of the signer. MUST appear in the envelope's `signers` array.

documentSha256.description: Hex-encoded SHA-256 of the document the signer attests to. MUST equal envelope.documentSha256 (defense against envelope tampering between request and sign).

webauthnCredentialId.description: Base64url-encoded WebAuthn credential ID used to sign. The credential is pre-registered against signer's DID via `com.etzhayyim.member.adherent` or a future passkey-registration record.

webauthnAlgorithm.description: COSE algorithm identifier of the WebAuthn key.

assertionEnvelope.description: XChaCha20-Poly1305 envelope (Signal key-wrap per ADR-2605181100) containing the WebAuthn assertion JSON ({clientDataJSON, authenticatorData, signature}). Encrypted-at-rest because clientDataJSON contains the challenge which is sensitive when correlated with envelope rkey.

challengeSha256.description: Hex-encoded SHA-256 of the WebAuthn challenge that was signed (replay defense — challenge MUST equal sha256(envelopeUri || signerDid || nonce)). Public so verifiers can recompute without decrypting the envelope.

userAgent.description: Optional client UA string at sign time. Metadata only — not authoritative.

signerAgentAuthorityRef.description: Optional AT URI of the signer's AAT (`com.etzhayyim.agent.authority`). Present when the signer is an AI agent acting under delegated authority; absent when the signer is a human Adherent signing in their own capacity. Per ADR-2605231500. Verifiers MUST check that the AAT scope covers the envelope's purpose at sign time.
